title: Devissage of coherent sheaves by integral closed subschemes (Stacks 01YI)
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] such that (0) $\mathcal P$ holds for the zero module; (1) for any short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, if two out of the three have property $\mathcal P$ then so does the third; (2) for every integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] closed subscheme $Z\subset X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with generic point $\xi$ there exists some coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ such that (a) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=Z$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2), (b) the stalk $\mathcal G_\xi$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is annihilated by the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\xi\subset\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ [def-weil-residue-field], (c) $\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal G_\xi=1$, and (d) property $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal G$. Then property $\mathcal P$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.12.6 (Tag 01YI, label lemma-property, coherent.tex line 3270); hypothesis (0) is added here because without it the lemma fails for X empty (then (1) and (2) hold for the property 'false'); for X nonempty (0) follows from (1) and (2) applied to 0->G->G->0->0

proof.text: Property P is invariant under isomorphism by applying (1) to $0\to0\to F'\to F\to0$ and using (0). A finite filtration by coherent submodules whose successive quotients have P therefore has P on its total module by induction; the empty filtration is covered by (0).

source.place: Lemma 01YI proof after the statement; finite-filtration induction

proof.text: For every coherent $\mathcal F$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] supplies a finite filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal F_m=\mathcal F$ by coherent submodules with $\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}\cong(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$ for closed immersions $i_j:Z_j\to X$ with $Z_j$ integral and nonzero coherent ideals $\mathcal I_j\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_j}$. Let $\eta_j$ be the generic point of $Z_j$. Since $i_j$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed set $i_j(Z_j)$, the stalk of $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$ at $i_j(\eta_j)$ is $(\mathcal I_j)_{\eta_j}$, which is nonzero by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] (a)$\Rightarrow$(c). As $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1})\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ (stalks of subquotients), every closed set containing $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ contains $i_j(\eta_j)$ and hence its closure $i_j(Z_j)$, an irreducible closed subset of $X$.

Call an irreducible closed subset $T\subseteq X$ good when $\mathcal P$ holds for $i_*\mathcal I$ for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ with $Z$ integral and $i(Z)=T$ and every quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$. Suppose some irreducible closed subset is bad. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] applied to the set of bad irreducible closed subsets there is a minimal bad $T_0$, together with an integral $i_0:Z_0\to X$, $i_0(Z_0)=T_0$, and an ideal $\mathcal I_0$ such that $\mathcal P$ fails for $(i_0)_*\mathcal I_0$; every irreducible closed subset strictly contained in $T_0$ is good.

source.place: Lemma 01YI proof ('If this fails, then since X is Noetherian there is a minimal integral closed subscheme Z_0')

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-coherent-property-irreducible] with $T=T_0$ to the restriction of $\mathcal P$ to coherent modules with support in $T_0$. Its (1) is the item's (1) for sequences whose terms are supported in $T_0$; its (2) holds because for integral $i:Z\to X$ with $i(Z)\subsetneq T_0$ the set $i(Z)$ is irreducible closed and good by minimality (step 3); its (3) is the item's (2) applied to the integral closed subscheme $Z_0$, whose generic point is that of $T_0$. The lemma gives $\mathcal P$ for every coherent module supported in $T_0$, in particular for $(i_0)_*\mathcal I_0$, whose support lies in $i_0(Z_0)=T_0$: a contradiction. Thus every irreducible closed subset is good.

source.place: Lemma 01YH (label lemma-property-irreducible, coherent.tex line 3179), invoked in the proof of Lemma 01YI

proof.text: Filter an arbitrary coherent $\mathcal F$ as in step 2. Each quotient $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$ has $\mathcal P$ because $i_j(Z_j)$ is good (step 4), so $\mathcal F$ has $\mathcal P$ by step 1 (for $m=0$, i.e. $\mathcal F=0$, by (0)).
